newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: West Africa ministers seek end to Haj health curbs.
newsitem.headline: West Africa ministers seek end to Haj health curbs.

text.p: Health and interior ministers from West African nations hit by meningitis epidemics this year have asked Saudi Arabia to lift restrictions on their citizens wanting to make the Moslem Haj and other pilgrimages to Mecca.
Ministers from Niger, Nigeria, Chad, Mali, Algeria and host Burkina Faso made the call on Friday in a statement issued at the end of a two-day meeting.

The ministers also agreed on measures to help curb outbreaks of meningitis, which killed up to 16,000 people between January and September in the region, as well as other diseases such as cholera, measles and yellow fever.
The ministers described the Saudi restrictions as "unjustified from a public health point of view" and asked their governments to put pressure on the Saudi government to lift the curbs.
Saudi Arabia stopped many of their nationals travelling to the holy Moslem sites on its territory earlier in the year, citing the meningitis epidemics as the reason.

The ministers agreed to implement basic measures such as vaccination campaigns to curb outbreaks in individual countries and to promote cooperation in the sub-region in the fight against such illnesses.
